correctness.rationale: An exact block decomposition reduces the second projection to an idempotent block \(D\) and a free rectangular block \(C\), with \(\operatorname{rank}(FE)=\operatorname{rank}C\). The exact Gaussian rank counts yield a positive-definite two-variable saddle and its five-residue Euler/theta limit. Restricting \(C=0\) yields a distinct saddle and the \(q^{-2n^2/15}\) modulus-fifteen prefactor; no weak-limit step is misused for this rare event. The mixed square-zero flag count cancels to the exact Euler-product ratio \(\Phi_{n-2s}/\Phi_{n-s}\), giving the same full asymptotics. Dominated convergence and tightness establish total variation; direct finite arithmetic and matrix multiplication were replayed from the actual packaged checker. The result holds for every fixed prime-power field order and every ambient dimension along the specified residue classes.

The joint lattice limit identifies tightly coupled factor ranks and the conditional reverse-product defect; the sharp \(q^{-2n^2/15}\) rarity and modulus-fifteen constant quantify the phase separation between one- and two-sided zero products. The cross-ensemble asymptotic equivalence is a structural relation between distinct idempotent and square-zero constraints. This is not merely another finite count, a trivial normalization, or an arbitrary narrow slice.
